## Reaction rates by mass action (`reactions`) {#sec-ch06-mass-action}

### Summary

The kinetics module turns a list of reactions into one rate per reaction. Each rate is a rate constant times the
product of the reactant concentrations raised to their stoichiometric coefficients. The species tendency is the
stoichiometric matrix times the vector of rates. Every other scheme of this chapter supplies either a rate constant
or a replacement for the mass-action product.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Reaction rates $r_j = k_j \prod_i c_i^{\nu_{ij}}$, @eq-ch06-mass-action-rate.

**Data.** Temperature [K], pressure [Pa], molar concentrations [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$] in, rates [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$] out.

**Placement.** `Kinetics.forward`, called by the driver once per step.

**Activation.** The `reactions` block of the YAML file; always on when it is present.

**Guarantee / limits.** Pointwise and exact for the given rate constants; concentrations floored at $10^{-300}$.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $c_i$, molar concentration of species $i$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$]; $k_j$, rate constant of reaction
$j$ (units set by the reaction order); $\nu_{ij} \ge 0$, forward order of species $i$ in reaction $j$ [-];
$S_{ij}$, net stoichiometric coefficient of species $i$ in reaction $j$ [-] (products positive, reactants
negative); $r_j$, rate of reaction $j$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$].

The scheme is always on. Reversible reactions are split into a forward and a reverse column; the reverse rate
constant is the forward one divided by the equilibrium constant from the NASA-9 data of @sec-ch02.

### Derivation

**Why a rate is a product of concentrations.** An elementary reaction is a single collision event. The number of such
events per unit volume and time is proportional to the number density of each partner that must meet, so for a
reaction whose reactant $i$ appears $\nu_{ij}$ times the event rate is proportional to $\prod_i c_i^{\nu_{ij}}$. The
proportionality factor is the rate constant $k_j$, which depends on temperature (and, for the fall-off forms, on
pressure) but not on the concentrations of the reactants:

$$
r_j = k_j(T, p) \prod_i c_i^{\nu_{ij}} .
$$ {#eq-ch06-mass-action-rate}

@eq-ch06-mass-action-rate is computed in `forward_with_rate_constants`
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}}), with the orders $\nu_{ij}$ held in
the buffer `forward_orders`, equal to the reactant coefficients except for evaporation columns
(@sec-ch06-evaporation).
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch06-mass-action-rate check_ch6_rates.py [a1] -->
Since $r_j$ is in $\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$ and each concentration in
$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$, a reaction of total order $n_j = \sum_i \nu_{ij}$ has $k_j$ in
$(\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}})^{1 - n_j}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; @sec-ch06-arrhenius converts the input units to these.

**From rates to tendencies.** Each event of reaction $j$ changes the amount of species $i$ by $S_{ij}$ (products
positive, reactants negative). Summing over reactions,

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d} c_i}{\mathrm{d} t} = \sum_j S_{ij}\, r_j .
$$ {#eq-ch06-mass-action-tendency}

@eq-ch06-mass-action-tendency is formed by the caller, for example as `stoich @ rate`, with $S$ the `stoich` buffer
built in `reset` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::reset >}}).

**Reversible reactions as two columns.** For a reversible reaction `reset` appends a second column $-S_{\cdot j}$ to
the stoichiometry. Its rate $r_{\bar j} = k_{\bar j} \prod_i c_i^{\nu'_{ij}}$ uses the product coefficients
$\nu'_{ij}$ as orders. The two columns together contribute
$S_{ij} r_j + (-S_{ij}) r_{\bar j} = S_{ij}(r_j - r_{\bar j})$ to @eq-ch06-mass-action-tendency, the net rate of
the reaction.

**Atoms are conserved exactly.** Let $a_{e i}$ be the number of atoms of element $e$ in species $i$. A balanced
reaction has $\sum_i a_{e i} S_{ij} = 0$ for every element, and so does its negated reverse column. The element total
$\sum_i a_{ei} c_i$ then has the tendency

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t} \sum_i a_{ei} c_i = \sum_j \Big(\sum_i a_{ei} S_{ij}\Big) r_j = 0 ,
$$

whatever the rate constants are, because the inner sum vanishes column by column. The check confirms both the rate
formula and $a S = 0$ to round-off.[^ch06-check-a]

**Reverse rate constants from the equilibrium constant.** Detailed balance states that at chemical equilibrium every
elementary reaction runs as fast forward as backward, $r_j = r_{\bar j}$. With the orders above this reads
$k_j \prod_i c_i^{\nu_{ij}} = k_{\bar j} \prod_i c_i^{\nu'_{ij}}$, and since $S_{ij} = \nu'_{ij} - \nu_{ij}$,

$$
\frac{k_j}{k_{\bar j}} = \prod_i c_i^{\,S_{ij}} \Big|_{\mathrm{eq}} .
$$

The right-hand side is fixed by thermodynamics. For an ideal gas the chemical potential of species $i$ at partial
pressure $p_i = c_i \mathcal R T$ is $\mu_i = g_i^\circ(T) + \mathcal R T \ln(c_i \mathcal R T / p_{\mathrm{ref}})$,
with $g_i^\circ$ the molar Gibbs energy at the reference pressure $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ (the kinetics option
`Pref`[^rg-f6026102f8bb],
default 101325 Pa). At equilibrium the reaction Gibbs energy vanishes, $\sum_i S_{ij} \mu_i = 0$. Dividing by
$\mathcal R T$ and moving the reference terms to the right gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_i S_{ij} \ln c_i &= -\frac{\Delta g_j^\circ}{\mathcal R T} - \Delta n_j \ln\frac{\mathcal R T}{p_{\mathrm{ref}}} \\
\Delta g_j^\circ &= \sum_i S_{ij}\, g_i^\circ(T) \\
\Delta n_j &= \sum_i S_{ij}
\end{aligned}
$$

so the equilibrium product is the concentration equilibrium constant

$$
\ln K_{c,j} = -\frac{\Delta g_j^\circ}{\mathcal R T} + \Delta n_j \ln\frac{p_{\mathrm{ref}}}{\mathcal R T} ,
$$ {#eq-ch06-mass-action-kc}

computed in `forward_with_rate_constants`
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}}) from the NASA-9 polynomials.
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch06-mass-action-kc check_ch6_rates.py [d1] -->
Detailed balance then fixes the reverse rate constant as

$$
k_{\bar j} = \frac{k_j}{K_{c,j}} .
$$ {#eq-ch06-mass-action-reverse}

@eq-ch06-mass-action-reverse is computed in the same function
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}}). There $g_i^\circ/(\mathcal R T)$ comes
from the NASA-9 polynomials (`nasa9_gibbs_RT`, @sec-ch02-nasa9), $\Delta n_j$ is the buffer `dn` built in `reset`, and
$K_{c,j}$ is clamped below at $10^{-250}$ before the division. Because @eq-ch06-mass-action-reverse holds at every
state, a state where all reversible reactions balance satisfies $\prod_i c_i^{S_{ij}} = K_{c,j}$, which is the
chemical-equilibrium condition of @sec-ch05: the fixed point of the kinetics is the chemical equilibrium. The check
compares $k_j/k_{\bar j}$ from the code with an independent $K_{c,j}$ from the NASA-9 data file at 300 K and 1500 K
(both NASA-9 ranges) and finds the forward and reverse rates equal to round-off at such a state.[^ch06-check-d1]
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch06-mass-action-reverse check_ch6_rates.py [d1] -->

**Temperature derivative of the reverse rate constant.** Taking the logarithm of @eq-ch06-mass-action-reverse and
differentiating,

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d} \ln k_{\bar j}}{\mathrm{d} T} = \frac{\mathrm{d} \ln k_j}{\mathrm{d} T} - \frac{\mathrm{d} \ln K_{c,j}}{\mathrm{d} T} .
$$

The first term of @eq-ch06-mass-action-kc changes with $T$ by the Gibbs-Helmholtz relation,
$\mathrm{d}(g^\circ/\mathcal R T)/\mathrm{d}T = -h^\circ/(\mathcal R T^2)$, and the second by $-\Delta n_j/T$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm{d} \ln K_{c,j}}{\mathrm{d} T} &= \frac{\Delta h_j^\circ}{\mathcal R T^2} - \frac{\Delta n_j}{T} \\
&= \frac{\Delta h_j^\circ - \Delta n_j \mathcal R T}{\mathcal R T^2} = \frac{\Delta u_j^\circ}{\mathcal R T^2} ,
\end{aligned}
$$

using $h = u + \mathcal R T$ for each ideal gas, so that $\Delta h^\circ - \Delta n\, \mathcal R T = \Delta u^\circ$
(the
van 't Hoff equation in concentration units). Multiplying the first relation by $k_{\bar j}$,

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d} k_{\bar j}}{\mathrm{d} T} = \frac{1}{K_{c,j}} \frac{\mathrm{d} k_j}{\mathrm{d} T}
- k_{\bar j} \frac{\Delta u_j^\circ}{\mathcal R T^2} .
$$ {#eq-ch06-mass-action-reverse-dt}

@eq-ch06-mass-action-reverse-dt is the correct temperature derivative. At the code pin `forward_with_rate_constants`
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}}) stores
$\mathrm{d} k_j/\mathrm{d}T$ itself in the reverse column, without the factor $1/K_{c,j}$ and without the second term
(see Limits). The concentration derivative is divided by $K_{c,j}$ correctly. The check measures the forward
derivative against a finite difference, and confirms that the reverse entry is off by exactly the predicted
amount.[^ch06-check-d2]
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch06-mass-action-reverse-dt check_ch6_rates.py [d2] -->
<!-- equation-source: eq-ch06-mass-action-reverse-dt code differs (D65) -->

No published derivation is quoted. The steps above are textbook chemical thermodynamics,[^ch06-kee] checked against
the code at the pin.

### Numerical method

The rate constants of all reaction forms are evaluated first, one evaluator module per form, in the fixed order
Arrhenius, coagulation, evaporation, three-body, Lindemann, Troe, SRI, KB fall-off. Each evaluator runs under
autograd on a copy of the concentrations, so its derivative $\partial k_j / \partial c_i$ comes back with the rate
constant (and $\partial k_j / \partial T$ when `evolve_temperature` is set). Concentrations are floored at
$10^{-300}$ ($10^{-30}$ in single precision) before the power, so that $0^0$ and $r_j / c_i$ stay finite. Evaporation
columns replace the product by the condensate concentration alone (@sec-ch06-evaporation). A finite entry of the
optional input `kf_override` replaces the computed rate constant and zeroes its concentration derivative.

The figure of the evaluator order is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| options | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp KineticsOptionsImpl >}} | `KineticsOptionsImpl` | `reactions` |
| YAML reader | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics_options.cpp KineticsOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}} | `from_yaml` | `reactions` |
| stoichiometry, evaluators | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::reset >}} | `reset` | always |
| rates | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}} | `forward_with_rate_constants` | always |
| Python binding | {{< code python/csrc/pykinetics.cpp bind_kinetics >}} | `bind_kinetics` | always |

: Code map of mass-action rates. {#tbl-ch06-mass-action-code}

1. `from_yaml` reads `reference-state`[^rg-1ffc2d860575] (`Tref`[^rg-782fd094d3ef], `Pref`) and then each reaction
family from `reactions`; reactants
   and products are sorted into vapor and cloud species, vapors first.
2. `reset` builds `stoich` (species by reaction, reversible reactions appended as negated columns), registers one
   evaluator per family, and builds `forward_orders`, in which an evaporation column has order one in its
   condensate and zero in its gases.
3. `forward_with_rate_constants` returns the rates, $\partial k / \partial c$, the optional $\partial k / \partial
   T$, and the raw rate constants; `forward` returns the first three.

The tolerances of the Chapman-cycle tests are missing evidence: they have not been read for this draft. CPU and
CUDA instantiations of `test_kinetics` exist; run records are not attached yet. The derivation checks run four
reactions, including `2 H => H2` and a termolecular one, for `[a1]` and `[a2]`, which measure 0 for both. `[d1]` runs
`O + O2 <=> O3` and `O + O3 <=> 2 O2` at 300 K and 1500 K and measures at most $1.1 \times 10^{-14}$ in the committed output; a second machine at the same pin gives
$2.8 \times 10^{-14}$, a round-off difference. `[d2]`
measures $2.4 \times 10^{-10}$ for the forward column. Its reverse line is an expected failure: the code gives
$-81.9$ where the true $\mathrm{d}k_{\bar j}/\mathrm{d}T$ is $4.8 \times 10^{-8}$, and the difference equals the
predicted $\mathrm{d}k_j/\mathrm{d}T - \mathrm{d}k_{\bar j}/\mathrm{d}T$ to $2.4 \times 10^{-10}$.[^ch06-check-d2]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- With `evolve_temperature` on, the reverse columns of $\partial k/\partial T$ are a copy of the forward ones. They lack
  the factor $1/K_{c,j}$ and the term $-k_{\bar j}\,\Delta u_j^\circ/(\mathcal R T^2)$ of
  @eq-ch06-mass-action-reverse-dt ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}}).
  The reverse-column derivative, and with it the temperature-feedback Jacobian of @sec-ch06-jacobian, is therefore
  generally incorrect for reversible reactions. This includes $K_{c,j} = 1$ whenever $\Delta u_j^\circ \ne 0$,
  because the van 't Hoff term is still missing; the copy agrees only where $K_{c,j} = 1$ and
  $\Delta u_j^\circ = 0$. Where $K_{c,j}$ is far from 1 the error is far larger than the van 't Hoff term alone ($-81.9$ against $4.8 \times 10^{-8}$ in the check). This is a recorded code defect with a fix in progress;[^ch06-d65] the derivation above is the
  intended result.
- $K_{c,j}$ is clamped below at $10^{-250}$, so a reverse rate constant cannot exceed $10^{250} k_j$.
- The reverse columns are added only when the options carry NASA-9 data. The stoichiometry gets its reverse columns
  whenever a reaction is reversible, so a reversible reaction without NASA-9 data would leave the rate vector
  shorter than `stoich` has columns. Read from `reset` and `forward_with_rate_constants`; that this fails at the
  `stoich @ rate` product is a hypothesis, not run.
:::

[^ch06-d65]: [source: UCzhangxi/kintera#54, row D65 (reverse-reaction `rc_ddT` entries: the $1/K_c$ factor and the
    van 't Hoff term). This text is to be updated when that fix merges.]
